archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: Dynamic-slot subprocess spawning in a loop with silent failure fallback and no stderr diagnostic capture is the highest-risk new code path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `_dynamic_slot_rows` in `python/plan_review_panel.py`: each dynamic slot spawns a `render plan-review` subprocess per iteration, captures stdout, and silently falls back to an empty rendered string on non-zero exit — subprocess stderr is not captured or logged anywhere. Assess whether failed render calls produce actionable diagnostics (e.g. appended to `execution-issues.md`), whether per-slot subprocess spawning in a tight loop can exhaust resources for manifests with many archetypes, and whether the `body_file` write → subprocess read ordering is race-free in all call contexts. Also check whether `proc.stdout` on a zero-exit but empty render is distinguishable from the non-zero-exit fallback, and whether `_slot_row` with an empty rendered string silently discards the slot or propagates a detectable degraded signal. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: The new --body-file path relaxes --archetype validation and adds a second validation chain; the overlap between _scope_anchor_common_shape_ok and _validate_design_prompt_file and the slot-name-to-filename construction deserve structural review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the `--body-file` code path in `python/rendering.py` `render_plan_review_main`: the archetype constraint is relaxed when `args.body_file` is truthy, and the body file is validated first by `_scope_anchor_common_shape_ok` (size, readability, non-symlink) then by `_validate_design_prompt_file` (CR/LF in path, symlink, confinement). Assess whether the two validation calls overlap, contradict, or leave a gap — particularly whether a symlink that passes `_scope_anchor_common_shape_ok` can still escape confinement before `_validate_design_prompt_file` fires. Also inspect `_dynamic_slot_rows` in `python/plan_review_panel.py`: `slot` is derived from the scout manifest's `name` field (stripped but not sanitized for path separators); check whether `round_dir / f"{slot}.body"` can escape `round_dir` when `name` contains `/` or `..` components. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
